rounds.text: Incap Ltd trades at an extraordinarily demanding P/E of 137 [E1] (or 141.44x compared to the sector benchmark of 99.44x [E6]), despite recent price growth running 80% ahead of actual profit growth [E55]. This inflated valuation coincides with fundamental underperformance, highlighted by a negative return on assets of -4.93% that trails the sector benchmark of -4.25% [E8], alongside decelerating earnings growth [E71]. Long-term growth remains virtually nonexistent, as evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of just 1% [E14] and trailing twelve month sales growth contracting by -6% [E17], underscoring why 5-year sales growth of 8.66% is flagged as poor [E62]. Reflecting these persistent operational drag factors, the stock sits at just 28% of its 52-week price range [E5]. Conceded: [E16] and [E66] demonstrate recent growth acceleration, with 3-year compounded sales growth reaching 15% [E16] and YoY sales surging +66% [E66]. However, short-term sales spikes cannot offset a decade of overall top-line stagnation and negative asset returns while the stock trades at such extreme earnings multiples [E1], [E8], [E14].
